question: At the pinned TRL #7249 base and head, does the real Trainer accumulation path preserve a full-window token-mean policy objective and its gradients/optimizer update under uneven completion-token microbatches, with simulated cross-rank aggregation?

estimand.policy_loss: sum of active per-token losses over every rank and microbatch divided by total active completion tokens over the optimizer accumulation window
estimand.gradient: gradient of that token-mean objective; distributed gradients are averaged across ranks
estimand.auxiliary_loss: not a primary token-mean claim; the PR intends to retain the existing equal-microbatch scale and the test fixture has a constant auxiliary scalar

contract_boundary: The protocol tests the token-mean estimand asserted by TRL issue #7206 and PR #7249. It does not prove that this is the only valid objective for every AsyncGRPO use case.

method.execution: Run the exact focused test file added by PR #7249 against the immutable candidate source, then run the same test file against the immutable base source without modifying either trainer implementation.
primary_tests: accumulated loss and gradients versus full-batch reference for unequal/equal/zero token counts and accumulation windows
simulated cross-rank gradient averaging against full-batch reference
one actual Trainer optimizer update versus the full-batch reference
method.model: The PR's deterministic token-local CPU test model; no pretrained weights or generated data.

failure_criteria: Any source revision, source file hash, or test hash differs from the lock.
The candidate focused test file has an unexplained failure.
The base test execution does not expose a failure attributable to uneven token-count accumulation, or the candidate fails the same relevant assertion.
The test requires a GPU, paid API, or externally hosted model.
limitations: No real pretrained model, asynchronous rollout worker, optimizer training run on task data, or downstream capability metric.
The rank test simulates DDP averaging in one process; no real multi-process distributed run.
The focused test file is part of the PR under review, so this is independent execution and source audit, not an independently authored test suite.
The constant auxiliary-loss fixture does not establish equivalence for token- or batch-dependent MoE auxiliary losses.
